docs.title: Helper CLI
docs.text: This page provides documentation for our command line tools.

docs.title: helper
docs.text:
Usage:

helper [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

Options:

Name Type Description Default -V, --version boolean Show the version and exit. False --help, -h boolean Show this message and exit. False

Subcommands

  • all: Show all info
  • arch: Display system architecture information.
  • docker: Docker container and image management.
  • env: Manage environment variables.
  • file: File management and processing commands.
  • internal-ip: Display the local/internal IP address.
  • nixos: NixOS related commands.
  • public-ip: Display the public (external) IP address.
  • run: Run predefined command snippets.
  • speed: Test internet speed using speedtest.net
  • system-info: Display system information including CPU, RAM, and disk usage
  • venv: Manage Python virtual environments.

Usage:

helper all [OPTIONS]

Name Type Description Default --help, -h boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: helper arch
docs.text:
Display system architecture information.

Shows the machine hardware name, which is useful for determining if you're running on x86_64, arm64, or other architectures.

Equivalent to running 'uname -m' in the terminal.

Example: $ h arch arm64

Usage:

helper arch [OPTIONS]

Options:

Name Type Description Default --help, -h boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: helper docker
docs.text:
Docker container and image management.

Manage Docker containers and images with subcommands for common operations.

Subcommands: ps List containers run Run a command in a new container rm Remove one or more containers rmi Remove one or more images url Show containers with their HTTP/HTTPS URLs

Examples: h d ps # List running containers h d run nginx # Run an nginx container h d rm container # Remove a container

Usage:

helper docker [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

Options:

Name Type Description Default -v, --verbose integer range (0 and above) Increase verbosity (can be used multiple times) 0 --help, -h boolean Show this message and exit. False

Subcommands

  • ps: List containers.
  • rm: Remove one or more containers.
  • rmi: Remove one or more images.
  • run: Run a command in a new container.
  • url: Show containers with their HTTP/HTTPS URLs.

docs.title: helper docker ps
docs.text:
List containers.

Usage:

helper docker ps [OPTIONS]

Options:

Name Type Description Default --all, -a boolean Show all containers (default shows just running) False --all-containers boolean Show all containers (default shows just running) False --format, -f choice (table | json) Output format table -h, --help boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: helper docker rm
docs.text:
Remove one or more containers.

Usage:

helper docker rm [OPTIONS] [CONTAINERS]...

Options:

Name Type Description Default --force, -f boolean Force the removal of a running container (uses SIGKILL) False --volumes, -v boolean Remove anonymous volumes associated with the container False --help, -h boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: helper docker rmi
docs.text:
Remove one or more images.

Usage:

helper docker rmi [OPTIONS] [IMAGE]

Options:

Name Type Description Default --all-tags, -a boolean Remove all versions of the image with the given name False --force, -f boolean Force removal of the image False --no-prune boolean Do not delete untagged parents False --help, -h boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: helper docker run
docs.text:
Run a command in a new container.

Usage:

helper docker run [OPTIONS] [IMAGE]

Options:

Name Type Description Default --name text Assign a name to the container Sentinel.UNSET --port, -p text Publish a container's port(s) to the host Sentinel.UNSET --detach, -d boolean Run container in background and print container ID False --env, -e text Set environment variables Sentinel.UNSET --volume, -v text Bind mount a volume Sentinel.UNSET --help, -h boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: helper docker url
docs.text:
Show containers with their HTTP/HTTPS URLs.

Usage:

helper docker url [OPTIONS]

Options:

Name Type Description Default --show-all, -a boolean Show all containers (default shows just running) False --http-only, -h boolean Show only containers with HTTP/HTTPS ports False --help boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: helper env
docs.text:
Manage environment variables.

Usage:

helper env [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

Name Type Description Default --help, -h boolean Show this message and exit. False

Subcommands

  • get: Get environment variable(s).
  • list: List all environment variables in a formatted table.
  • set: Set an environment variable.

  • unset: Unset an environment variable.

docs.title: helper file
docs.text:
File management and processing commands.

Usage:

helper file [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

Options:

Name Type Description Default --directory, -d directory Directory to search in (default: current directory) . --extension, -e text Filter by file extension (without dot) Sentinel.UNSET --size, -s boolean Show file sizes False --modified, -m boolean Show last modified time False --help, -h boolean Show this message and exit. False

Subcommands

  • newest: Show the newest files in the directory.
  • oldest: Show the oldest files in the directory.

docs.title: helper internal-ip
docs.text:
Display the local/internal IP address.

This command shows the internal (LAN) IP address of your machine. It automatically detects the correct network interface based on your OS.

Examples: $ h ip 192.168.1.100

Note: On multi-homed systems, this shows the primary network interface's IP.

Usage:

helper internal-ip [OPTIONS]

Options:

Name Type Description Default --help, -h boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: helper public-ip
docs.text:
Display the public (external) IP address.

This command retrieves and displays your public IP address as seen from the internet. It's useful for checking your current external network identity.

Examples: $ h pubip 203.0.113.45

Note: Requires an active internet connection. Uses ifconfig.me service by default.

Usage:

helper public-ip [OPTIONS]

Options:

Name Type Description Default --help, -h boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: helper run
docs.text:
Run predefined command snippets.

Usage:

helper run [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

Options:

Name Type Description Default --help, -h boolean Show this message and exit. False

Subcommands

  • add: Add or update a snippet.
  • edit: Edit snippets file directly in your default editor.
  • exec: Execute a snippet with the given arguments.
  • list: List all available snippets.
  • remove: Remove a snippet by name.
  • show: Show the command template for a specific snippet by name or index.

docs.title: helper run add
docs.text:
Add or update a snippet.

Example: h run add click-odoo "docker exec {ODOO_CONTAINER} bash -c "click-odoo {file}""

Note: {container} will be automatically converted to {ODOO_CONTAINER} and {db_container} to {ODOO_DB_CONTAINER}

Usage:

helper run add [OPTIONS] NAME [COMMAND]...

Options:

Name Type Description Default --help, -h boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: helper run edit
docs.text:
Edit snippets file directly in your default editor.

Usage:

helper run edit [OPTIONS] [EDITOR]

Options:

Name Type Description Default --help, -h boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: helper run exec
docs.text:
Execute a snippet with the given arguments.

Examples: h run exec click-odoo /path/to/script.py h run exec 1 /path/to/script.py h run exec --force 1 /path/to/script.py

Usage:

helper run exec [OPTIONS] SNIPPET [ARGS]...

Options:

Name Type Description Default -f, --force boolean Skip confirmation prompt False --help, -h boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: helper venv
docs.text:
Manage Python virtual environments.

Usage:

Options:

Name Type Description Default --help, -h boolean Show this message and exit. False

Subcommands

  • deactivate: Deactivate the current virtual environment.
  • source: Source a Python virtual environment.

docs.title: helper venv deactivate
docs.text:
Deactivate the current virtual environment.

Usage: h venv deactivate # Show the deactivate command eval $(h venv deactivate) # In bash/zsh to deactivate the virtual environment

Usage:

helper venv deactivate [OPTIONS]

Options:

Name Type Description Default --help, -h boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: helper venv source
docs.text:
Source a Python virtual environment.

If no path is provided, searches for a virtual environment in the current or parent directories. Looks for 'venv' first, then '.venv'.

Usage: h venv source [PATH] # Source the specified virtual environment or auto-detect eval $(h venv source) # In bash/zsh to activate the virtual environment source <(h venv source) # Alternative syntax for bash/zsh

Usage:

helper venv source [OPTIONS] [PATH]

Options:

Name Type Description Default --help, -h boolean Show this message and exit. False
